assumption: Operators guides and local actors will discuss feasibility
supporting_evidence: Guidor public directory confirms multilingual guide supply across English, German, French, Spanish and other languages; Amsterdam rules define guided-tour operating constraints. Willingness, availability and commercial terms remain untested. Article 07 verifies a public professional-guide sourcing route through Guidor and an optional Hortus group-tour pathway; actual quote/availability remain open.

assumption: At least one route can meet accessibility and public-space requirements
supporting_evidence: Article 06 produced an accessibility variant and Article 07 makes field audit a mandatory release condition; current public infrastructure evidence supports feasibility but does not validate surfaces/kerbs end to end.
validation_method: Access audit and accompanied route test

assumption: A viable product can contribute beyond central concentration
supporting_evidence: Amsterdam policy explicitly supports positive city contribution and visitor dispersal; 2025 carrying-capacity evidence shows pressure in six neighbourhoods, but no specific product geography is validated. Article 06 finds four strong dispersal-compatible corridors; Article 07 default concept uses Plantage→Oosterpark without depending on the highest-pressure centre.
